sd_latchstrings_the.blurb: A hillside of limestone boulders in Spearfish Canyon, up the slope from a roadside pullout. This is a bouldering-only spot with 18 problems that cover a wide spread, from an easy V1 through the middle grades and on to a handful of problems at V8 and V9. The blocks are short, roughly 10 to 15 feet, and the lines are steep with decent holds, so bring pads. The slope faces the sun, which helps on cooler days. It makes a good side trip if you are already climbing in the canyon and want something different from the sport walls.

sd_gully_of_biblical_proportions_the.blurb: A cool, fern-lined gully in the Mohican section of Spearfish Canyon, holding 17 bolted sport routes on limestone streaked in black and white. It is a hard-leaning venue: one route near 5.10, a handful in the 5.11s, most in the 5.12s, and a few at 5.13. The gully stays shaded and a breeze sometimes funnels through it, which makes it a reasonable pick when the sun-baked walls are too warm. It is not a place for beginners. The trail leads left past neighbouring walls, and the farthest-right lines are reached by crossing a narrow ledge.

sd_meat_counter.blurb: A compact cluster of formations in the Needles of the Black Hills near Mount Rushmore, set beside a big chockstone just past Chopping Block. About 17 problems and routes are packed into a small space, mixing short bolted sport lines, a few trad leads and boulder problems. Sport and trad climbs run from easy fifth class through the 5.10s with a couple of harder lines, and the boulders stretch from V4 up to a very hard V10. Many routes are short enough that a single rope handles the rappel. A good stop for a varied session rather than a long day.

sd_south_wall.blurb: A popular quartzite wall at Palisades State Park, close to Garretson in the east of the state, sitting upstream of Harkor Tower. Most of the 16 climbs are traditional leads on cracks, with two top-rope lines, and they range from about 5.5 to the low 5.11s, so it suits both newer climbers and stronger ones. Access to the top is easy, which makes rigging top-ropes simple. The rock here is slick with little friction, rewarding crimps and cracks. It is busy because it is so convenient, so an early start helps. Bolting is not part of the local ethic.
